expectation: pHH3 marks mitotic nuclei: sparse, bright, compact or condensed-chromatin nuclear signal in a few percent of cells. In this gut tissue these would be scattered single cells in the proliferative crypt or base of the epithelium, with stroma and muscle largely negative.
observed: A: signal follows the whole tissue, brightest along the epithelium and mucosal edges, with no sparse bright puncta. B: most cells are lit about alike, plus haze. C: signal sits at the apical and luminal edge and in stromal blobs, not on nuclei. D: yellow blobs sit beside the blue nuclei, not on them.
notes: HH3 lights the whole tissue outline and most epithelial cells at similar intensity. The brightest spots are luminal or stromal blobs that sit off the nuclei, and there are no sparse condensed mitotic nuclei in crypts.
why: Signal is broad and follows the tissue and epithelial density, with no distinct sparse nuclear mitotic population; the bright spots sit off the nuclei.
